document.title: Motion for Extension of Time, Shortened Answer Period and Request for Expedited Action of the Indicated PJM Transmission Owners

pages.text:
1 
UNITED STATES OF AMERICA 
BEFORE THE  
FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION 
PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., et al.

   EL25-49-001

MOTION FOR EXTENSION OF TIME, SHORTENED ANSWER PERIOD 
AND REQUEST FOR EXPEDITED ACTION 
OF THE  
INDICATED PJM TRANSMISSION OWNERS 
Pursuant to Rules 212 and 2008(a) of the Rules of Practice and Procedure of the Federal 
Energy Regulatory Commission (“Commission”),1 the Indicated PJM Transmission Owners2
(collectively the “PJM Transmission Owners”) respectfully request that the Commission grant 
a thirty (30) day extension of time for submission of (i) revisions to PJM Interconnection, 
1
18 C.F.R. §§ 385.212, 385.2008(a) (2025). 
2
For the purpose of this filing, the Indicated PJM Transmission Owners are: American Electric Power 
Service Corporation on behalf of its affiliates, Appalachian Power Company, Indiana Michigan Power Company, 
Kentucky Power Company, Kingsport Power Company, Ohio Power Company, Wheeling Power Company, AEP 
Appalachian Transmission Company, AEP Indiana Michigan Transmission Company, AEP Kentucky 
Transmission Company, AEP Ohio Transmission Company, and AEP West Virginia Transmission Company; The 
Dayton Power and Light Company d/b/a AES Ohio; Dominion Energy Services, Inc. on behalf of Virginia Electric 
and Power Company d/b/a Dominion Energy Virginia; Duke Energy Business Services, LLC for Duke Energy 
Kentucky, Inc. and Duke Energy Ohio, Inc.; Duquesne Light Company; East Kentucky Power Cooperative; Exelon 
Corporation on behalf of its affiliates Atlantic City Electric Company, Baltimore Gas and Electric Company, 
Commonwealth Edison Company, Commonwealth Edison Company of Indiana, Inc., Delmarva Power & Light 
Company, PECO Energy Company (“PECO”), and Potomac Electric Power Company; FirstEnergy Service 
Company, on behalf of its affiliates American Transmission Systems, Incorporated, Jersey Central Power & Light 
Company, Mid-Atlantic Interstate Transmission LLC, The Potomac Edison Company, Monongahela Power 
Company, Keystone Appalachian Transmission Company, and Trans-Allegheny Interstate Line Company 
(collectively, the “FirstEnergy Companies”); PPL Electric Utilities Corporation; Rockland Electric Company; and 
Southern Maryland Electric Cooperative.

2 
L.L.C.’s (“PJM”) Tariff “to require that the Eligible Customer taking transmission service on 
behalf of a Co-Located Load takes one of three transmission services[;]”3 and (ii) initial and 
reply briefs in the paper hearing that the Commission established in its order issued on 
December 18, 2025 in this proceeding4 to allow the PJM Transmission Owners to develop and 
propose new PJM-wide transmission rates and rate structures and to communicate and 
coordinate with PJM and other impacted parties and stakeholders, including the Organization 
of PJM States (“OPSI”) and the Consumer Advocates of PJM States.  This additional time will 
promote administrative efficiency and ultimately benefit the Commission and parties to this 
proceeding. 
The PJM Transmission Owners are authorized to state that the PJM Industrial Customer 
Coalition does not oppose this motion. 
I. 
BACKGROUND 
In the December Order, the Commission found “that PJM’s Tariff is unjust and 
unreasonable because it does not contain provisions addressing with sufficient clarity or 
consistency the rates, terms, and conditions of service that apply to generators serving Co-
Located Load and Eligible Customers5 taking transmission service on behalf of Co-Located 
Load.”6  Specifically, the Commission found PJM’s Tariff “unjust and unreasonable because it 
3
See PJM Interconnection. L.L.C., 193 FERC ¶ 61,217, at P 193 (2025) (“December Order”) (The three 
transmission services include: “(1) [Network Integration Transmission Service] NITS or a new interim, non-firm 
transmission service while Network Upgrades to provide full NITS service are constructed, (2) a new Firm 
Contract Demand transmission service, or (3) a new Non-Firm Contract Demand transmission service.  As a part 
of this compliance obligation, PJM must ensure a transmission service agreement that reflects the rates[,] terms, 
and conditions of these new transmission service options is available to Eligible Customers.”).
4
Id. 
5
All capitalized terns that are not otherwise defined herein shall have the meaning set forth in the PJM 
Open Access Transmission Tariff or Amended and Restated Operating Agreement of PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. 
6
December Order at P 2.

3 
does not include types of transmission service that reflect Eligible Customers taking service on 
behalf of Co-Located Loads that are willing and able to limit their use of the transmission 
system under certain conditions.”7  The Commission concluded that it is necessary for PJM to 
offer three new forms of transmission service under its Open Access Transmission Tariff 
(“OATT”), and identified these three new forms of transmission service as: (i) interim, non-
firm transmission service; (ii) Firm Contract Demand transmission service; and (iii) Non-Firm 
Contract Demand transmission service. 
The Commission also held that additional record evidence is needed to set the 
appropriate replacement rates, terms, and conditions for the three new forms of transmission 
service in PJM.  As a result, the Commission established paper hearing procedures and listed 
eleven questions that it asked the parties to address “with specificity.”8  The Commission set 
the date for filing any initial brief in Docket No. EL25-49-000 as on or before February 16, 
2026.  The deadline to file responses to PJM’s initial brief is March 18, 2026, and the deadline 
to file replies to those responses is April 17, 2026.9
I. 
MOTION FOR EXTENSION OF TIME 
An extension of time for the initial filing deadline10 is warranted because this proceeding 
involves highly complex and interrelated issues that require careful analysis and coordination 
between PJM, PJM Transmission Owners, and other PJM stakeholders.  In particular, the 
December Order requires PJM Transmission Owners to develop and propose new PJM-wide 
7
Id. 
8
Id. at P 219. 
9
Id. at P 220. 
10
Because February 16 is a federal holiday, the PJM ITOs understand that initial briefs would, without an 
extension, be due on February 17, the first business day after the deadline set forth in the December Order. See 18 
C.F.R. §§ 385.2007 (2025).

4 
transmission rates and rate structures11 and mandates compliance measures that will 
fundamentally alter existing tariff provisions and operational practices.  These changes 
implicate numerous technical, legal, and procedural considerations, including the integration of 
new transmission services with existing offerings under the PJM OATT, alignment with cost 
recovery mechanisms, and consistency with governing documents.  Addressing these 
compliance obligations demands extensive consultation among stakeholders, PJM, and other 
impacted parties, including OPSI and Consumer Advocates of PJM, as well as detailed 
evaluation of tariff revisions to ensure conformity with the Federal Power Act and Commission 
precedent.  Given the breadth and complexity of these issues, additional time is necessary to 
develop a comprehensive and accurate compliance approach that fully satisfies all legal and 
regulatory requirements.   
The PJM Transmission Owners respectfully request a 30-day extension to the deadline 
for filing (i) revisions to PJM’s Tariff to effectuate three new forms of transmission service for 
Co-Located Load; and (ii) initial briefs, which would also push out the deadline for filing reply 
briefs by 30 days.12  Good cause exists to grant this modest extension of time.  The three forms 
of transmission service required in the December Order are both new and unique to PJM.  As 
such, devising and developing a rate proposal to effectuate these brand new services will require 
11
These matters directly implicate PJM Transmission Owners’ contractual and Federal Power Act filing 
rights. See Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland Interconnection, 108 FERC ¶ 61,033 (2004) (approving 
Settlement Agreement, Docket No. OA97-261-006 et al. (filed Oct. 3, 2003), as modified by Modification of 
Settlement Agreement, Docket No. OA97-261-009 et al., §§ 3.2, 4.2(B); 4.3, 4.5 (filed Jan. 20, 2004 and corrected 
Jan. 23, 2004)  The Settlement Agreement is incorporated into PJM OATT, § 9 and the Consolidated Transmission 
Owners Agreement at § 7.3.1, PJM Interconnection, L.L.C., Rate Schedules, TOA, TOA-42 Rate Schedule FERC 
No. 42 (1.0.0) (“CTOA”).  Moreover, the PJM Transmission Owners have contractual rights and obligations to 
engage in coordination and consultation with PJM and the PJM Members Committee with respect to changes to 
other terms and conditions of the PJM OATT.   See CTOA, at § 7.5.1. 
12
As noted above, currently initial briefs are due on or before February 16, 2026 with responses to initial 
briefs due March 18, 2026, and the replies to those responses due April 17, 2026.   Under the 30-day extension, 
initial briefs would be due on March 18, 2026, responses to initial briefs would be due on April 17, 2026, and the 
replies to those responses would be due May 18, 2026.

5 
a significant amount of resources, time, and effort on the part of the PJM Transmission Owners. 
In addition, the PJM Transmission Owners will need to consult with PJM regarding issues that 
administration of the new rate designs could present.  Finally, the PJM Transmission Owners 
will need additional time to receive input from PJM stakeholders, and other impacted parties, 
including the OPSI and the Consumer Advocates of PJM States, regarding the new services 
rates and rate designs.   
The PJM Transmission Owners appreciate the Commission’s desire to move 
expeditiously to implement the new services required by the December Order.  However, given 
the complexity and timing of the December Order, as well as the need to coordinate among the 
PJM Transmission Owners and with PJM, a 30-day extension is a reasonable accommodation 
in order to provide the parties with adequate time to engage and develop a rate proposal 
necessary to implement the three new services.  No entity will be unreasonably prejudiced by 
this modest extension.  To the contrary, parties and other PJM stakeholders, as well as the 
Commission, will all benefit from a well-designed proposal, which this extension will help 
ensure. 
II. 
MOTION FOR SHORTENED ANSWER PERIOD AND EXPEDITED ACTION 
In light of the circumstances described herein, the PJM Transmission Owners request 
that the Commission shorten the period for answers to this Motion to three (3) days, making 
answers due no later than January 20, 2026.  The PJM Transmission Owners also respectfully 
request that the Commission expedite its consideration of this Motion and promptly issue an 
order immediately after the due date for answers has passed, but no later than January 21, 2026.  
The PJM Transmission Owners and other parties will benefit from the Commission’s

6 
expeditious decision so they can coordinate with stakeholders and other impacted entities and 
work effectively towards a well-designed proposal.  
III. 
CONCLUSION 
As discussed above, the PJM Transmission Owners respectfully request that the 
Commission grant a 30-day extension of time for the submission of (i) revisions to PJM’s Tariff 
to effectuate three new forms of transmission service for Co-Located Load; and (ii) initial and 
reply briefs in the paper hearing established by the December Order.  The PJM Transmission 
Owners also request that the Commission establish a shortened period for answers to this 
Motion and issue an order on this Motion as soon as possible, but no later than January 21, 
2026. 
Respectfully submitted, 
/s/ Michael Kunselman

CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE

Dated in Washington, D.C. this 14th day of January, 2026. 
/s/ Daniel Klein 
Daniel Klein 
Davis Wright Tremaine LLP
